summary: A 43-minute group call review. Chris Klevan and Ben Byrne play back a recent discovery call of Andrew's at 1.5x and coach him line by line. The prospect on the recording is unnamed here and discloses Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, reconstructive elbow surgery, a shoulder partially dislocated about a month earlier, a kneecap that pops when he walks, hip flexor and lower back pain, ADD, self-described obesity and fear of gyms. The coaching is entirely about emotional depth: hold space, show empathy, replace leading and binary questions with open-ended ones, and build enough emotional anchors that the prospect will not resist the $6K price. Chris also states his position that finances should not be probed on a fitness offer, and closes by coaching Kyla to convert a reschedule into a triage call.
notable: A prospect with Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, a reconstructed elbow, a shoulder partially dislocated a month ago and a dislocating kneecap is discussed for 40 minutes as a sales opportunity, and nobody at any point asks whether a clinician has cleared him for kettlebell training. Chris calls him 'a great prospect'; Ben says two pain points are 'enough to close this guy'.
Chris states the purpose of building emotional anchors explicitly: 'they're not going to scoff at $6K. It's genuinely just going to be like, damn, I don't have the money.'

Chris states he does not probe finances on a fitness offer — 'I don't really care about their finances unless they tell me straight up, I'm living down by the river' — which contradicts the six financial-picture questions the Objection C play in the playbook requires.

Chris describes converting emergency-only credit into a purchase: 'maybe they think they don't have a lot of money, but they have a $20,000 credit card sitting there that they're like, only for emergencies. And it's like, well, you think this is an emergency?' The prospect under review had just said money was tight enough to affect what he eats.

Setter coaching: Kyla is told not to simply action a reschedule the prospect requested but to call and triage him under the framing that 'we just don't schedule anybody in unless we make sure that 100% it works', because 'it'll help you get a set out of it instead of just a reschedule'.
Ben and Chris cite prior experience on Cole Gordon's team as the standard being coached to.

Andrew uses a slur while describing the questioning style he is being taught ('kind of being a little bit like a retard'); Chris redirects the term to 'childlike curiosity' but the moment is not otherwise addressed.
Useful process content: open-ended over binary questions, 'what do you mean' as the highest-value question, and Kyla's confirmation that silence produces disclosure.
